name: ChatComponentServerFacet_SetProfanityFilterEnabled
summary: The client tells the chat server facet whether its profanity filter is on. A 45-byte record with a 17-byte body: the shared two-u64 head, then ONE boolean byte. It is read by the shared optional/bool reader FUN_1425a3070, whose decode side REFUSES any byte >= 2 - so this is a strict boolean rather than a count, and the card can say so from the codec and not from the sample.
purpose: Carry the client's profanity-filter setting to the chat component so the server can apply the filter it is asked to apply. What the server does with the value is not measured.

created_when: the chat component pushes its profanity-filter setting
lifecycle.if_absent: the server never learns the client's filter setting. The capture sends it at seq 0x61

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): typed header 00 01 9d 40, i.e. type index 4125 = 0x101d. A client record carries the body at record offset 28: the 8-byte frame head and the 16-byte actor id precede the typed header, so a 17-byte body makes a 45-byte record.

fields.name: local_facet_id
fields.note: Measured db 84 a5 d6 31 d9 b3 3a = 0xdb84a5d631d9b33a. First u64 of the shared message head: the sending facet's own local id, the chat client facet. It is NOT the social facet's ce81136a2b7ad33e, so chat and social are separate components even though both deal with text.

fields.name: enabled_flag
fields.note: Measured 0x00, leaving nothing over: 16 + 1 = 17 exactly. The reader writes `*(char *)(param_1 + 0x20) != '\0'` as ONE byte, and its decode side FUN_1425a30b0 rejects any byte >= 2 - so the width and the strictness are both from the codec. What the flag SWITCHES is not measured: only the value 0 was captured, so the field is named for its role (an on/off setting named by the message type) and not for an observed behaviour.
